positions.name: Solstice Advanced Materials, Inc.

positions.catalyst: Tier 1 CORPORATE ACTION, NOT AN EARNINGS TRADE - THE CLEANEST SETUP IN TODAY'S BOOK: On 8/27 Solstice and Element Solutions mutually terminated their planned acquisition, and the Solstice board simultaneously authorized a $500M share repurchase - 5.6% of the $8.95B market cap. SOLS is +13.7% pre-market at 64.08 on a 64.00/64.10 book, a TEN-CENT spread, the tightest quote of any new position. The market is plainly telling you it did not want the deal and does want the buyback. This is the Honeywell specialty-materials spinoff (refrigerants, semiconductor materials, data-center cooling, nuclear), completed 10/30/2025, and it is 29% below its 90.80 high from 5/13 - a broken-deal bounce off a de-rated base, not an extended chart.
positions.risks: THE BUSINESS ITSELF IS NOT WHY THIS IS UP AND THAT IS THE WHOLE PROBLEM - Solstice guided full-year 2026 adjusted EPS to $2.45-$2.75 against a $2.93 consensus and sales to $3.9-$4.1B, citing higher operating costs, plant downtime and a messy transition to low-global-warming-potential refrigerants. Margins are under real pressure. A buyback pop on a company with deteriorating fundamentals typically has a short half-life, and 42.8x earnings is a rich multiple to pay for a chemicals business with those problems. This is also a ten-month-old public company with no long trading history to lean on and it just went ex-dividend on 8/27. Stop at -5%, take profit at +8%.

positions.name: SLB Ltd.
positions.exitRule: 1-3 day swing - exit 9/3 or on a 5% stop / 8% take-profit
positions.catalyst: Tier 1 GEOPOLITICAL SUPPLY SHOCK AND THE SINGLE BEST-CONFIRMED CHART ON THE TAPE: over the weekend US forces struck two missile launchers on Iran's Larak Island inside the Strait of Hormuz - the first confirmed American strikes on Iran since late July - and the IRGC retaliated against US bases in Jordan and the UAE. Brent rose 3.5% to $91.20 and WTI 3.5% to $86.30. SLB was the largest mover in the entire energy complex at +5.16%, closing at 60.2862 against a 60.46 intraday high that IS its new 52-week high, on 22.44M shares versus a 10.33M 30-day average - 2.2x relative volume, the heaviest of any name I priced today. Oilfield services carry the most operating leverage to a sustained crude bid, and this is the only energy name that both broke out and closed on its high.
positions.risks: THIS IS A HEADLINE TRADE AND HEADLINES REVERSE OVERNIGHT WITHOUT WARNING - a de-escalation statement, a ceasefire signal, or simply no follow-on strike Tuesday morning takes the entire 5% back before the open, and I cannot stop out of a gap. The Strait of Hormuz has been a live conflict zone since late February, so this is the latest round of an existing stalemate rather than a new war, and the market has faded several of these rounds already. SLB is closing at a 52-week high on a war premium, not on an earnings or backlog catalyst, which means there is no fundamental support under the price if crude gives back the move. It also goes ex-dividend 9/2, inside the holding window. Stop at -5%, take profit at +8%.
positions.driver: Tier 1: Strait of Hormuz strikes, Brent +3.5% to $91.20
